title: Iterative SDK Rollouts & Telemetry-Driven Feedback Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes an iterative, telemetry-driven process for rolling out changes to Redwood client SDKs (redwood-sdk-js, redwood-sdk-py, redwood-mobile). It combines a lightweight canary plan, concrete telemetry contracts, automatic quality gates, and a feedback loop from product/CS to prioritize follow-up work. Use this for any SDK change that affects runtime > behavioral change (new parameter, retry/backoff, batching, default opt-ins), packaging changes that touch curiosity metrics (bundle size, latency), or surface-area changes to APIs.

Goals
-----
- Reduce regressions shipped in SDK releases by adopting small, measurable rollouts.
- Make rollout decisions data-driven using a small set of high-signal metrics.
- Give product and support a systematic path to provide prioritized feedback that connects to telemetry.
- Provide reusable templates and queries so teams can run consistent checks across SDKs.

When to use this playbook
-----------------------
1. Non-trivial SDK behavioral change (retry semantics, new caching, KV management).
2. Changes to default options that could affect latency or correctness.
3. Packaging or transpilation updates that may affect mobile/app bundle sizes.
4. Feature flags or API surface changes that require client opt-in.

Roles & Ownership
------------------
- SDK author (owner): implements change, writes release notes, prepares telemetry.
- SDK oncall / platform: monitors rollout metrics and executes rollback if thresholds breached.
- Product manager: defines acceptance criteria and end-user signals.
- Customer Success (CS): collects qualitative reports and links incidents to telemetry IDs.
- DX (Developer Experience) reviewer: validates docs and quickstarts are aligned with changes.

Telemetry contract (required signals)
------------------------------------
All SDK rollouts MUST emit or surface the following signals for at least 72 hours following each stage:
- sdk.build.version: semantic version (string)
- sdk.feature.flags: list of flags active for client (array-as-string ok)
- request.latency_ms: p50/p95/p99 measured at client callsite (numeric)
- request.error_code: grouped by canonical error buckets (400, 401, 429, 5xx, client-timeout)
- kv.cache.hit_rate: % hits for client-side caching where applicable
- bundle.size_bytes: (mobile/web packaging changes)
- telemetry.sample_rate: effective sampling rate (for aggregated metrics)
- diagnostics.log_id: stable id to correlate support reports to traces

Implementation notes:
- Instrumentation should write events to dx-telemetry-pipeline using the standard sdk_event schema.
- For JS SDK, integrate with window.__redwoodTelemetry or use the @redwood/telemetry helper.
- For Python, use redwood.telemetry.emit_event(...).

Quality gates (automated)
------------------------
Define stage-specific pass/fail rule sets in the CI/CD release pipeline. Recommended gates: 
1) Canary stage (1% traffic / 3 days):
   - p95 latency regression <= 20% vs baseline
   - error_rate increase <= 50% relative (min 0.05% absolute)
   - no new 5xx spike > 3x baseline
2) Ramp stage (10% traffic / 2 days):
   - p95 latency regression <= 10%
   - error_rate increase <= 25%
   - support reports <= 2 for top 50 customers using SDK
3) Global stage (100%):
   - final manual check + automated sanity (smoke tests)

If any gate fails, the oncall must follow the Rollback Runbook (see Runbook section).

Canary rollout template (recommended):
-------------------------------------
- Stage A: Nightly internal dogfooding + CI artifacts available (0% external). Duration: 24 hours.
- Stage B (Canary): 1% external traffic (or 5% for low-volume customers), window: 72 hours.
- Stage C (Ramp): 10% traffic, window: 48 hours.
- Stage D (Full): 100% traffic, full rollout

Traffic targeting options:
- User cohort by API key tag (customer-tier: internal, dev, prod).
- Random sampling (deterministic by client-id) for fairness.
- Geo-based segments for region-sensitive changes.

Example feature-flag config (YAML)
---------------------------------
# Place in infra/feature-flags/sdk-rollouts.yaml
feature: sdk-optimistic-cache-v2
owner: sdk-team@example.com
description: Enable new optimistic fetch + client-side cache invalidation for SDKs
stages:
  - name: canary
    percent: 1
    duration_hours: 72
    notes: "Canary to internal customers and random sample"
  - name: ramp
    percent: 10
    duration_hours: 48
  - name: global
    percent: 100

API examples and snippet templates
---------------------------------
1) Simple call with explicit telemetry tag (JavaScript)
```
const rw = require('@redwood/sdk-js');
const client = rw.createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, telemetryTag: 'opt-cache-v2-canary' });
await client.generate({ prompt: 'Hello' });
```
2) Emitting a diagnostic event (Python)
```
from redwood import telemetry
telemetry.emit_event('sdk.diagnostic', {
  'sdk.version': '1.4.0-canary',
  'build_os': 'linux-x86_64',
  'bundle_size_bytes': 512000
})
```
3) Feature flag check (pseudo-YAML consumed by client at start)
```
flags:
  sdk-optimistic-cache-v2: true
```

Queries & dashboards (examples)
-------------------------------
- ClickHouse (analytics-db) example: p95 latency by sdk version
```
SELECT
  sdk_version,
  quantile(0.95)(request_latency_ms) AS p95_latency_ms
FROM sdk_events
WHERE event_time >= today() - 7
GROUP BY sdk_version
ORDER BY p95_latency_ms DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
- BigQuery example: error rate change (SQL)
```
SELECT
  sdk_version,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_error THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*) AS error_rate
FROM `analytics.sdk_events`
WHERE event_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY sdk_version
ORDER BY error_rate DESC
```
- Redwood Console dashboard: create a dashboard named "SDK Rollout - <feature>" with tiles: p50/p95 latency, error rate (overall + by code), support tickets linked by diagnostics.log_id, bundle size over time.

Runbook: unexpected degradation
-------------------------------
1) Alert fires (see thresholds below) -> page SDK oncall via PagerDuty -> start incident bridge.
2) Triage: quick check of dashboards, compare canary vs baseline, inspect top 5 calling customers.
3) If error rate > 3x baseline OR p95 latency > 2x baseline -> escalate to rollback.
4) Execute rollback: toggle feature-flag to previous stage (or pin SDK version in feature service).
5) Verify stabilization (metrics back to baseline for 30 minutes) -> close incident, open postmortem if customer impact occurred.

Automated alert thresholds (examples)
- p95 latency increase > 40% vs baseline (5m window)
- error rate increase > 200% relative and > 0.2% absolute
- > 5 new support tickets referencing diagnostics.log_id in 60m

Post-deployment evaluation checklist (to run after Full stage)
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Confirm telemetry sample integrity (no missing fields).
- Validate that p95 and error rates are within acceptance for 14 days.
- Review top 10 support cases and tag with telemetry ids.
- Update SDK release notes and quickstarts with any changed defaults.
- Schedule follow-up epic if regressions are non-trivial.

SDK release notes template (short)
--------------------------------
Title: SDK vX.Y.Z — optimistic cache (v2)
Summary: Small behavioral change: optimistic caching is now enabled behind feature flag `sdk-optimistic-cache-v2`.
Breaking changes: none.
Telemetry: sdk.version, sdk.feature.flags, request.latency_ms.
Migration: no changes required; opt-in via feature flag.

Developer checklist before Canary (author)
----------------------------------------
- [ ] Add telemetry emissions per contract.
- [ ] Add unit and integration tests for new behavior.
- [ ] Prepare feature flag config and targeting list.
- [ ] Draft release notes and quickstart snippets.
- [ ] Pre-register dashboard in Redwood Console and add to shared watchlist.

Customer-facing communications
-----------------------------
- Draft short email for customers in the canary cohort: describe change, how to opt-out, and how to surface issues (diagnostics.log_id).
- CS playbook: how to collect logs or reproduction steps and where to attach telemetry ids.

Appendix: example incident timeline (hypothetical)
-------------------------------------------------
- 2025-11-02 09:00 UTC: Canary deploy starts (1% traffic).
- 2025-11-02 10:45 UTC: Automated alert - p95 increased 55% in last 15m.
- 2025-11-02 10:50 UTC: SDK oncall paged; bridge created.
- 2025-11-02 11:05 UTC: Triage shows error spike from particular customer (api-key=abc123).
- 2025-11-02 11:20 UTC: Rollback executed (feature flag disabled).
- 2025-11-02 11:55 UTC: Metrics trending back to baseline; incident closed.
